subject: Post-call: parity probe and test plan for tool-calling, structured outputs, streaming
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Amira Sayeed <amira@acuityhealth.com>, sales@cloudeval.com
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-14T09:02:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call recap + proposed probe for parity tests (tool-calling, streaming, structured outputs)

Hi Amira — thanks again for the time this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can align engineers on the same test matrix: 

TL;DR: Acuity wants a short, reproducible probe comparing Redwood hosted/dedicated -> Cloud vendor endpoints with an explicit focus on three buckets: 1) function/tool (tool-calling) fidelity and payload size, 2) structured output (JSON schema correctness + validation), and 3) streaming behavior/latency under realistic token budgets.

What we covered:
- You prioritize consistent output format (healthcare JSON schemas) and low tail latency for interactive clinician workflows.
- Procurement needs simple pass/fail acceptance criteria we can hand to legal/security and engineering.
- You have an internal eng contact (Amir H.) who will run tests and share results.

Proposed probe (owners + ETA):
- Tool/function calling correctness: run 150 distinct calls (varying argument types, nested JSON, 2–3 tool endpoints). Owner: Ben C. ETA: 5 business days for first run.
- Structured-output validation: run 200 prompts against target FHIR-like schema, measure schema-parse accuracy and post-processed validation errors. Owner: Jordan B. ETA: 5 business days.
- Streaming behavior: measure token-start latency, early-token streaming, partial-result stability (p50/p95) at 256/1024 token windows. Owner: Ben + infra. ETA: 7 business days.

Acceptance criteria we propose to feed procurement (simple pass/fail):
- Function calling: >95% correct mapping of tool args for the curated set; explicit examples for failures.
- Structured outputs: >=90% schema-parse success or fixable deterministic transforms.
- Streaming: p95 token-start latency < 250ms in our hosted region, with stable prefixes delivered in order.

Attachments: I dropped a starting probe matrix to Drive (acue-probe-matrix-20260514.xlsx) and the call recording. I also attached initial test scripts we plan to run.

Next steps I need from you:
1) Confirm Amir H.'s email so we can invite him to the Drive folder and Slack channel.
2) Confirm whether you want us to include Redwood Dedicated in the initial run or only hosted endpoints.
3) Any embargo/IDP rules for sample PHI-like payloads (we will supply synthetic, but want to respect policy).

If that looks good I will create the HubSpot note and schedule an internal test kickoff with Ben and Jordan for EOD tomorrow.

— Stephanie
Stephanie Nguyen
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com
(415) 555-0123

Subject: Re: Post-call recap + proposed probe for parity tests (tool-calling, streaming, structured outputs)

Thanks Stephanie — this is great and exactly the sort of structure procurement asked for. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Please include Redwood Dedicated in the initial comparison; our ops team prefers to see both hosted and dedicated options for latency/cost tradeoffs.
- Amir Hussein (amir.hussein@acuityhealth.com) will be our engineer lead — please share the Drive folder and any API keys or test harness instructions via our SSO link or a secure temp token.
- For sample payloads: we will only allow synthetic PHI (nonsensical identifiers). If you could send one synthetic sample that mirrors our real schema that would be ideal.

We can commit an Eng resource to run the test harness this week — I will block a half-day on Friday for an initial run. Can your infra/bench team be available then to iterate?

Amira
Amira Sayeed

Acuity Health
amira@acuityhealth.com
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Amira Sayeed <amira@acuityhealth.com>
Date: 2026-05-14T13:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + proposed probe for parity tests (tool-calling, streaming, structured outputs)

Adding technical detail for the probe so all parties have measurable tests to run. I'll own the test harness and initial runs. High-level plan: 

1) Benchmarks to collect (per endpoint: Redwood-hosted, Redwood-dedicated, CloudEval-managed):
   - Latency: token-start + full-response p50/p95/p99 at 256, 512, 1024 token targets.
   - Throughput: sustained tokens/sec and inference QPS under 1–8 concurrent streams.
   - Cost proxy: tokens-per-invocation * unit cost (we'll label but procurement will validate).

2) Function/tool-calling probe:
   - 150 calls split across simple flat args (60), nested args (60), streaming-tool-calls with partial tool payloads (30). Verify correct argument mapping + schema adherence.
   - Failure modes: truncated JSON, off-by-one tokenization, tool pointer mismatches. We'll log raw model outputs and parsed tool payloads.

3) Structured output: 
   - Use 200 prompts, validate against the provided FHIR-lite schema. Measure: parse-success, post-parse transform rate, number of manual fixes required. We'll also include a strict-JSON mode to stress the model.

4) Streaming/partial output: 
   - End-to-end token-start latency measurement at cold/warm cache. Include KV-cache warm-up scenario (simulating long chat sessions).
   - Validate incremental partial JSON streaming behavior for the clinician UI (must not produce twice-escaped JSON fragments).

Test artifacts & reproducibility:
- I will publish a tarball with the harness (test-scripts.tar.gz), docker-compose for the probers, and a small set of synthetic payloads that match your schemas.
- Suggest we run initial pass Friday morning PT; Jordan and I will be available to debug.

Ask: Jordan, can you draft the HubSpot note and create a Drive folder with editor access for Amira + Amir? Stephanie, can you confirm whether procurement requires a signed addendum for test access keys?

— Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

Thanks all — quick operational next steps from my side: 

1) I created the Drive folder and uploaded the probe matrix + a template HubSpot note: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/0ABC123. Amira, I invited amir.hussein@acuityhealth.com as an editor.
2) HubSpot deal ACU-1459 updated with test plan and expected timeline (link: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/ACU-1459).
3) Friday run: Ben will kick off at 09:00 PT. Jordan & Ben will monitor infra; Stephanie will coordinate with procurement. Please confirm if Friday 09:00 PT works for Amir.
4) I'll collect first-pass artifacts and post raw results to the Drive (results/ folder). If we hit any outright regressions vs CloudEval, we'll flag for an immediate follow-up with product engineering.

If we get clean passes on function-calling and structured-output, procurement is comfortable moving forward with the pilot contract.

— Jordan
